author: Ebanski
quote: Looks incredible. Plays great. The physics are legit. The story? Damn near unbearable. I refunded **** used to be an anarchy simulator. Steal cars, blow stuff up, cause chaos, get distracted doing some ridiculous nonsense just because you could. Now we’ve got Chore Simulator 2026. Painting walls, buying necklaces, earning relationship points. Come on, **** spare me the “it’s optional” argument. The activities might be optional, but the relationship is baked into the story. Can I dump Lucia? Date somebody else? Cheat? Nope. Funny how Grand Theft Auto, of all games, suddenly has **** New York Times praised the game for exploring “the work required” to make relationships successful. Man, I didn’t buy GTA to do relationship work.Then there’s Jason. Army veteran, drug runner, capable with guns, boats, and airplanes, yet he’s constantly taking orders from Lucia. Meanwhile, her introduction involves leaving their baby in a coffee shop to attempt a botched robbery that gets her arrested. So why is she suddenly calling the shots? If Rockstar wants her running the show, fine, but make it believable. Jason barely feels like a protagonist. He’s just there to follow instructions and manage her **** whole thing feels preachy. The ideology is forced, the writing is heavy-handed, and the anything-goes attitude that made GTA what it was seems to have taken a back seat. The world is incredible, but the story keeps dragging me into a relationship I have no interest in **** V, Red Dead Redemption 2, and Cyberpunk 2077 all told better stories. Cyberpunk is still getting updates. If I just want gunfights, I’ve got Bodycam and Ready or Not.Thirteen years for a gorgeous world and a story I couldn’t stand. GTA in name only.Thank God for the modders. Can’t wait until they turn this into something worthwhile.Oops. Not supposed to say that.I meant I’ll patiently wait for the PC release and GTA Online, and maybe then I’ll give it another shot.
